final_answer:
MSA DEVIATION REPORT - NEXORA REDLINE (Ashford Merritt, 14 Apr 2025) v. TEMPLATE v4.2 / PLAYBOOK v3.1
To: P. Narayanan (GC); D. Whitfield (AGC). Privileged; do not share externally.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Do not sign on this redline. At least 16 changes breach Tier 1 or beyond-fallback Tier 2 limits and need written GC approval (Playbook 5.5-5.6; 48-hour GC turnaround). Likely hard "no" items: (1) data-breach liability triad; (2) Vendor ownership of ML models trained on PHI; (3) offshore residency; (4) BAA 60 days after signing; (5) loss of incident-triggered audit; (6) 12-month claims bar. The cover email understates the markup: it says the cap "remains at 2x annual fees" (redline: 1x fees actually paid in 6 months), calls residency "minor", and never mentions the 75% termination fee, 5% SLA cap, deleted audit right, deleted M&A assignment right, Feedback license, cyber cut, 48-hour notice, NDA incorporation or publicity right. The tracked "base" also departs from v4.2 (section 3). Target signing is 30 May 2025; escalate Tier 1 items now and plan a principals call (Pryce/Caldwell).

2. LEDGER (Clause | Redline | Playbook | Risk | Counter | Approver)

A1. LIABILITY TRIAD - 8.1(b), 9.1-9.3 (PB 3.1-3.4, 4). CRITICAL.
- Cap: 2x paid-or-payable/12 months becomes 1x actually paid/6 months; multiplier, lookback and basis all cut (GC). SOW fees are quarterly in advance ($362,500/quarter), so the cap is about $362,500 at month 3 and $725,000 at month 6 (implementation milestones, $385,000 total, may add), below the Playbook's $1,000,000 first-year floor. Preferred: $2,900,000.
- 9.2: data-protection/confidentiality carve-out deleted, and the 8.1(b) indemnity carve-out silently dropped; only IP indemnity, willful misconduct/fraud and Customer payment remain.
- New "Super Cap" 2x annual SOW fees (about $2.9M Y1), excluding 8.1(b). Floor is the greater of 3x annual fees (about $4.35M) or TCV ($4,481,805 platform; $4,866,805 with implementation). Not met.
- 8.1(b): negligence becomes gross negligence (no fallback) plus a $3,000,000 aggregate cap, below TCV; its interplay with the 9.1 cap is unclear.
- 9.3: data-breach and confidentiality carve-outs deleted, so notification costs, OCR/AG penalties and class-action costs are likely excluded as consequential.
- Combined analysis (PB 4.4): PB 4.3 scenario losses are $22M-$70M; under the redline recovery is about $362,500 direct damages, and the indemnity fails absent gross negligence (an unpatched-vulnerability breach is ordinary negligence).
- Counter: restore template 8.1(b), 9.1, 9.2, 9.3. Fallbacks: cap 1.5x/12 months/paid-or-payable; data-breach super cap at least greater of 3x annual fees or TCV, with negligence trigger, defense (or reimbursement with interim cost cover) and consequential carve-out kept. Approver: GC.

A2. IP / ML - 7.1(b)-(d), 7.2(b), 7.3, 6.5 (PB 3.5). CRITICAL.
- 7.1(d): Vendor owns models/weights "developed or refined using Customer Data", reusable for other customers. Of the four mandatory fallback safeguards only a bare "no Customer Data or derivatives" proviso appears (weights trained on PHI may encode it); no exclusion of customer-specific models, no HIPAA Safe Harbor certification (45 CFR 164.514(b)), no competitor covenant. Any gap defeats the fallback.
- 7.2(b): worldwide license to use Customer Data "to improve and develop Vendor's products", contradicting the email's "segregation" claim. 6.5: Vendor keeps "de-identified or aggregated" data; a business associate may de-identify only if the BAA permits (45 CFR 164.502(d), 164.504(e), unverified), and hospital BAAs may bar it.
- 7.1(b) now "subject to" Vendor IP; 7.1(c) keeps "improvements ... in connection with the Services"; template 7.1(d) Customer Data ownership is missing. 7.3: perpetual, irrevocable Feedback license without the template's Customer Data limits.
- Counter: delete 7.1(d), 7.2(b) additions, 6.5 retention; restore Customer ownership of Customer Data, Output and Customer-specific models; fallback is the four-safeguard model; limit Feedback. Approver: GC.

A3. RESIDENCY - 6.4 (PB 3.6). CRITICAL.
- "Other jurisdictions as Vendor may designate" with "substantially similar" standards and 30 days' notice: a named escalation trigger, no fallback. "Continental", the bar on remote access/processing from abroad, and the warranty are dropped.
- Reeves memo 5.1: Nexora's Singapore environment gives engineers production-data access and is outside the Thorngate SOC 2 (only Northern Virginia and Oregon); Caldwell's "development and testing only" assurance is undocumented. Verdantis's 14 hospital BAAs require US-only processing.
- Counter: restore template 6.4 (access, all environments, subprocessors); require written disclosure and remediation of Singapore access before signing. Approver: GC (approval unlikely).

A4. BAA - 1.4, 6.2, Exh. C, 14.10 (PB 3.7). CRITICAL.
- "Mutually acceptable" BAA within 60 days of the Effective Date: named trigger. Reeves expects PHI 3-4 weeks after signing (SOW migration weeks 4-9; SOW 12(d) assumes BAA first), so PHI would flow with no BAA, violating 45 CFR 164.502(e)/164.504(e); subcontractor BAA terms must match hospital BAAs.
- Counter: Verdantis's standard BAA (template Exhibit A, removed) signed with the MSA. Fallback: binding condition precedent barring PHI disclosure/access until execution. Reject 14.10 ranking the BAA last (contradicts 6.2); BAA controls for PHI. Approver: GC.

A5. AUDIT - 11.1-11.3 (PB 3.11; Reeves 5.3). CRITICAL.
- Vendor may satisfy audits with a SOC 2 that Customer "shall accept"; incident-triggered audit at Vendor's expense deleted; template 11.2(b) (third-party auditors) and 11.2(d) (remediation/follow-up) silently absent. Each is a trigger. The SOC 2 excludes Singapore.
- Counter: restore template 11.2. Fallback: SOC 2 for the annual audit only if scope covers all environments (including Singapore), plus supplemental audit on deficiencies and full incident-triggered audits. Approver: GC.

A6. CONFIDENTIALITY - 5.1-5.6 (PB 3.16). Tier 2, escalate.
- General survival 3 years: acceptable (AGC). Trade-secret survival fixed at 5 years and no PHI/Customer Data carve-out (template 5.3 treating Customer Data as Confidential Information is missing): GC. Counter: indefinite for trade secrets, PHI, Customer Data.
- Mutualize 5.1 (only Vendor pricing/architecture/roadmap); reject Affiliate disclosure (Singapore) and retention under Vendor policy (5.5) for Customer Data.

B1. TERMINATION FOR CONVENIENCE - 10.2, Exh. A item 8 (PB 3.8). HIGH.
- Customer-only right; Vendor's right deleted; fee 75% of remaining fees: over the 50% maximum and unilateral (each a trigger). End of Year 1: remaining $3,031,805; fee $2,273,854; paid plus implementation plus fee $4,108,854 = 84.4% of $4,866,805 (91.7% of platform TCV). End of Year 2: fee $1,153,729; total $4,482,229 (92.1%). Presumptive excess is over 75%.
- Counter: bilateral right; fee 25%/15%/0% stated in the SOW (currently silent). Fallback: up to 50% declining, total under 75% of TCV. Approver: GC beyond fallback.
- Also reject 10.5(e) (licenses end immediately, conflicting with SOW 10.2's 90-day transition); template 10.4 transition clause missing; data return 30 becomes 60 days; 10.5(f) survival omits Section 6.

B2. SLA - 4.1-4.4 (PB 3.12). HIGH.
- Credits capped at 5% of annual fees (about $72,500 Y1), below the 10% trigger (fallback at least 15%, about $217,500), "notwithstanding any SOW", overriding SOW 7.2 (up to 30% of a month's fee; $36,250 at 94%) and 7.4. Two bad months exhaust it. Template 4.3(e) (material-breach exception) removed; reports monthly to quarterly (conflicts SOW 9.1); 4.4(e) excuses third-party providers (would cover Nexora's hosts).
- Counter: no cap, or at least 15%, with sole remedy for routine misses only, persistent-failure termination, 4.3(e) restored; reject 4.4(e). Approver: GC below 10%.

B3. CURE - 10.3 (PB 3.13). HIGH. 45 days for all breaches plus extension "as is reasonably necessary" with no outer limit: trigger. Counter: 30 days; fallback 45 plus at most 30 (75 total), none for security/PHI breaches; keep 10-day payment cure. Approver: GC (extension).

B4. LAW/FORUM - 13.1-13.4 (PB 3.10). HIGH. California law (disfavored; Cal. Civ. Code 1668 uncertainty); binding arbitration before the "Western Arbitration Council" (non-standard, strongly disfavored), seated San Francisco (Vendor's home), no punitive damages; mediation and Durham courts deleted: triggers. Counter: North Carolina, or Delaware (both parties are Delaware entities; AGC); mediation then Durham courts. Fallback: AAA/JAMS seated in Durham or neutral, no remedy limits, court equitable relief. The deleted jury waiver is not in v4.2 and the Playbook disfavors waivers: accept deletion. N.C. Gen. Stat. 22B-3 relevance unverified. Approver: GC.

B5. LIMITATIONS - 9.5 (PB 3.9). HIGH. 12 months from accrual "regardless of when known", all claims including data, indemnity, IP; NC default is 3 years (N.C. Gen. Stat. 1-52(1), per Playbook). Counter: delete; fallback at least 24 months from discovery, excluding data/HIPAA, indemnity and IP. Approver: GC.

B6. ASSIGNMENT - 14.3 (PB 3.14). HIGH. M&A/sale carve-out deleted (trigger); Affiliate assignment kept with weaker liability wording. Counter: restore with written assumption; fallback non-competitor, 30-day notice, creditworthiness, consent not unreasonably withheld; Vendor Affiliate assignees must meet US-residency/BAA terms. Approver: GC.

B7. INSURANCE - 12, Exh. B (PB 3.19). HIGH. Cyber $10M to $5M: absolute floor; the $7.5M fallback applies (TCV under $5M), so $5M needs GC. Also additional-insured "where commercially available", cyber additional insured/primary-noncontributory and tail dropped (template 2 years; Playbook 3), certificates 10 business days after Effective Date, not at signing. Exhibit B cyber row blank; Pinnacle limits undisclosed (Reeves). Counter: $10M or $7.5M; certificate before execution. Approver: GC.

B8. WARRANTIES/INDEMNITY - 2.1, 3.1-3.3, 8.1(a), 8.2(d) (PB 3.17). MEDIUM-HIGH. 3.2(a) "generally accepted practices" acceptable (AGC). 3.2(b) "commercially reasonable" security without NIST/HITRUST/ISO reference needs GC; counter adds a framework. Reject the "to Vendor's knowledge" non-infringement qualifier, template-absent 3.2(g) malware warranty omission, 2.1 conditioning performance on Customer compliance, and new 8.2(d) Customer indemnity for the "content, accuracy, or legality" of Customer Data (limit to third-party IP claims as in template 8.2(a)). 8.1(a) exclusions: acceptable with tightening.

B9. FORCE MAJEURE - 13.5 (PB 3.18). 120-day trigger exceeds 90 (GC); termination "may", SOW-only; restore whole-Agreement right. Pandemic and sanctions additions acceptable (AGC). Exclude cyber events and subprocessor failures; extension acceptable only up to 30 days; add fee abatement (fees are paid in advance); security/BAA duties not suspended.

C1. PAYMENT - 2.3 (PB 3.15). Net 30 acceptable (AGC); SOW 4.4 says Net 45 from receipt, so conform. 18% interest exceeds 12% (GC); fallback lesser of WSJ prime plus 2% or 10%, undisputed sums, 15-day grace, savings clause. 15-day dispute notice and tax wording already in template: accept.

C2. SECURITY/SUBPROCESSORS - 6.1, 6.3, 6.6, Exh. C. Subprocessor consent becomes notice plus a 15-day objection with no veto; PHI subprocessors require consent and BAA flow-down (fallback: 30 days' notice, US-only, objection with termination right). Incident notice 24 to 48 hours: Playbook silent; Nexora's incident plan says "without unreasonable delay"; counter 24, and check hospital BAAs before conceding. "Security Incident" undefined once BAA separated. Restore "appropriate" safeguards and template 6.3/6.6 (RCA, credit monitoring). Exh. C "periodic" pen testing contradicts annual (template, SOW 8.2(d)); Exhibit C SOC 2 "[DATE]" blanks.

C3. OTHER. NDA (10 Feb 2025) incorporated and in 14.1: not in file; obtain, and state MSA Section 5 controls. 14.11 Customer name/logo use: reject. "Execution Version" label: reject. 1.18/1.21 undefined service types and Affiliates: conform. Accept 14.5, 14.6, 14.8, 14.9.

3. RED FLAGS
(a) Redline base text diverges from v4.2 without tracking, so treat all as untracked: template 6.2 condition precedent, 6.3, 6.6, 6.4 warranty, 7.1(d), 8.1(b) loss list, 8.1(c)-(d), 5.3, 3.2(b),(g),(h), 2.3(f), 14.1 subcontracting consent, 11.2(b),(d) absent; Exhibit A changed from BAA to SOW form; Exhibits B-C new; base includes a jury waiver and 30-day mediation absent from v4.2. Demand a full machine comparison against clean v4.2.
(b) Email conflicts with redline (cap, residency, "customary" limitations, indemnity "refined").
(c) Playbook cites 8.2(b) for data-breach indemnity; template and redline use 8.1(b).
(d) SOW: Net 45, annual pen testing, SOC 2 full-scope (Nexora cannot meet) and "no ETF" overrides conflict with MSA 2.2/14.10 (MSA prevails unless SOW expressly supersedes); SOW cites MSA 10.1 as "Termination for Cause" and 10.3 as "Cure" (wrong).
(e) Memo ties 30 May to "Q2 FY2025" with a 30 June year-end: confirm the budget-lapse date.

4. NEXT STEPS
1. Today: written Tier 1 escalation memo to GC (PB 5.2) for A1-A6, B1-B7.
2. Counter-markup on clean v4.2 and a list of unflagged changes to Ashford Merritt.
3. Tell Reeves and Koh that BAA at signing gates PHI; residency and audit are hard no's.
4. Before signing, obtain Singapore access documentation, full-scope SOC 2, cyber certificate and the NDA.
5. Principals call within about 10 days.
